No further proof promised is an awkward negative promise-status claim; the input contains no prior Crown promise and an empty evidence plan, but a present refusal to promise unsupplied proof would be clearer.

Actors 2-4 compress departure with the token into remaining in hand and describe direct conflict. The accounts create credibility tension; absent continuous observation or timing, they do not independently establish nonoccurrence of a handover. These responses still attribute both accounts and assess doubt rather than find no handover as fact.
